Postmodernism is a literary movement that emerged in the mid-to-late 20th century, characterized by a skepticism toward grand narratives, objective truth, and traditional structures. In literature, it often employs techniques such as metafiction (where the work draws attention to its own artificiality), fragmentation, non-linear timelines, intertextuality, and irony. It challenges the idea that a single, authoritative meaning exists within a text, instead suggesting that meaning is constructed, unstable, and dependent on the reader’s interpretation.
